title: Remove Every Node With a Given Value
statement: `head` is the head of a linked list. Remove **every node whose value equals `val`** and return the head of the resulting list (which can be empty). Re-link the existing nodes; do not build a new list.

examples.explanation: Every node is removed: the list becomes empty.

hints.nudge: Removing the first node is different from removing a node in the middle, because there is no node before the first one. Can you avoid the special case?
hints.pattern: A dummy node in front of the head; walk with a pointer to the node BEFORE the one you inspect, and skip the next node when it has the value.
hints.pseudocode:
dummy.next = head; prev = dummy
while prev.next:
  if prev.next.val == val: prev.next = prev.next.next
  else: prev = prev.next
return dummy.next
hints.walkthrough: To delete a node you must change the `next` of the node before it. The head has no such node, which is why you add a dummy node in front: now every real node has a predecessor, and the answer is dummy.next at the end (it also works when the whole list is removed). Keep `prev` on the last node that stays. Look at prev.next: if it has the value, unlink it (prev.next = prev.next.next) and look at the new prev.next without moving prev (several equal nodes in a row must all go); otherwise move prev forward. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) memory.
